# #298 — P1: Prove backup-chain and restore compatibility across upgrades and replay

State: OPEN
Author: rodaddy
Labels: enhancement, memory, closure-audit
Created: 2026-07-19T02:21:12Z
Updated: 2026-08-05T22:43:28Z

---

Parent: #293

## Problem
A local settings restore script and one successful smoke do not establish durable recovery. First-class memory needs recovery objectives, chain integrity, clean-environment restore drills, version compatibility, and defined ordering with pending spool replay.

## Acceptance criteria
- Define RPO, RTO, retention, encryption, integrity, and off-host independence requirements.
- Detect missing, corrupt, incomplete, drifted, or incompatible backup-chain elements before mutation.
- Record schema, package/runtime version, namespace/scope model, source provenance, and index/embedding compatibility metadata.
- Restore regularly into a clean environment and verify namespace isolation, exact scopes, session continuity, schema compatibility, and usable retrieval.
- Test old backup to upgraded runtime, backup during upgrade, interrupted upgrade, rollback, restore followed by replay, and client reconnect.
- Define deletion/redaction/retention semantics so replay or restore cannot resurrect prohibited or retired data.
- Generate one current one-command restore after every activation/upgrade rather than accumulating a fragile manual restore chain.
- Emit content-free backup, verification, restore, and rollback receipts; alert on stale backups and failed drills.

## Evidence
The Claude rollout required two activation manifests and a chained restore script after follow-up fixes.
